_note: Places and links. Names are in plain words, with the ship's own term in brackets where the record uses it. name is what you call your own cabin; alias is how anyone else's reads. about: one plain line on what and where the place is. deck: G (lowest) up through F, E, D, C, B, A to Boat (the top, where the lifeboats hang). at: [x, y] on the side-on silhouette, bow to the right (larger x is further forward). side: port (left, facing the bow) or starboard (right). Moves are described from deck, at and side. open: an open deck (caught there when it floods or at 02:20, you go into the water; below decks, you go down with her). floodsAt: the place is lost from then on. knownTo: the classes who would know the place by name and the way to it; anyone else sees only which way a move goes until they have been there (the boat deck was first- and second-class space; third class had the well decks and the poop, BR-3rd). sees: from this open place you can see the boats at that end of the boat deck (fwd or aft). Barriers hold a class back until a time, up to holdMax minutes: delay and detour, never a wall. Source: docs/twenty-boats-research.md sections 4 and 5.

cabin-1.name: Your cabin, first class, C deck
cabin-1.about: First-class cabins in the middle of the ship, three decks below the lifeboats.

cabin-2.name: Your cabin, second class, D deck, at the back
cabin-2.alias: Second-class cabins, D deck, at the back
cabin-2.about: Second-class cabins towards the back of the ship, four decks below the lifeboats.

cabin-3-fwd.name: Your bunk, third class, G deck, at the front
cabin-3-fwd.alias: Third-class bunks, G deck, at the front
cabin-3-fwd.about: Shared bunk rooms near the bottom of the ship, right at the front, where the iceberg struck. The lifeboats are seven decks up.

cabin-3-aft.name: Your cabin, third class, E deck, at the back
cabin-3-aft.alias: Third-class cabins, E deck, at the back
cabin-3-aft.about: Shared third-class cabins low down at the back of the ship. The lifeboats are five decks up.

grand-staircase.name: The Grand Staircase
grand-staircase.about: The great first-class staircase under a glass dome. It runs from the cabins straight up to the lifeboats.

promenade-a.name: Covered walkway, A deck (the promenade)
promenade-a.about: A long first-class walkway along the side of the ship, one deck below the lifeboats.

smoking-room.name: First-class smoking room
smoking-room.about: A first-class lounge towards the back, one deck below the lifeboats.

stairs-2.name: Second-class stairs and library
stairs-2.about: The main second-class staircase, towards the back. It goes up to the lifeboats.

scotland-road.name: Long crew corridor, E deck ("Scotland Road")
scotland-road.about: A wide passage low in the ship, running most of its length. Crew and third class used it to get between the front and the back.

general-room-3.name: Third-class common room
general-room-3.about: A plain sitting room for third class, near the back of the ship.

well-deck-fwd.name: Open deck at the front (forward well deck)
well-deck-fwd.about: A small open-air deck near the front, sunk below the decks around it. Third class used it for air. The lifeboats are three decks up.

well-deck-aft.name: Open deck at the back (after well deck)
well-deck-aft.about: An open-air deck near the back, sunk below the decks around it. The lifeboats are three decks up.

boat-deck-fwd-port.name: Lifeboat deck, front, left side (port)
boat-deck-fwd-port.about: The top deck, where the lifeboats hang. This is the front end, on the left side as you face the front. Sailors call the left side port.

boat-deck-fwd-stbd.name: Lifeboat deck, front, right side (starboard)
boat-deck-fwd-stbd.about: The top deck, where the lifeboats hang. This is the front end, on the right side as you face the front. Sailors call the right side starboard.

boat-deck-aft-port.name: Lifeboat deck, back, left side (port)
boat-deck-aft-port.about: The top deck, where the lifeboats hang. This is the back end, on the left side as you face the front. Sailors call the left side port.

boat-deck-aft-stbd.name: Lifeboat deck, back, right side (starboard)
boat-deck-aft-stbd.about: The top deck, where the lifeboats hang. This is the back end, on the right side as you face the front. Sailors call the right side starboard.

stern.name: The very back of the ship (the poop deck)
stern.about: A raised open deck at the very back of the ship. There are no lifeboats here.

links._route: Hart's route forward along C deck past the second-class library

barrier.what: the emergency door to second class
stewards at the stairs up from the open deck

links._route: climbing the cargo crane and over the rail

barrier.what: a gate at the top of the stairs to the first-class deck
